# file-triage-demo

Scans a folder of copied documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, photos, and archives in **strictly read-only mode** and produces a plain-English triage report explaining which files will not open, why, and what to do next safely.

**Strictly read-only:** the scanner only reads file metadata and byte ranges. It never moves, renames, repairs, encrypts, or deletes any file in the scanned folder.

**All data here is synthetic.** "Alder & Pine Studio", its clients, and all 60 sample files are generated by [`src/sample.js`](src/sample.js). No real personal or client files are in this repo.

**See the output without running anything:**
[`output/triage-report.md`](output/triage-report.md) · [`output/triage-report.html`](output/triage-report.html) · [`output/triage-report.csv`](output/triage-report.csv) · [ground truth](samples/truth.json)

## Why this exists

After migrating an old laptop, restoring from an external drive, or downloading a shared cloud folder, files often show up with familiar names and icons yet refuse to open. Before paying for recovery software or deleting anything by mistake, a business owner needs a clear inventory separating healthy files from empty stubs, misnamed downloads, cut-off transfers, and password-locked files.

## Sample of the report

Excerpt from [`output/triage-report.md`](output/triage-report.md):

```markdown
## Summary

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| Files scanned | 60 |
| Healthy files (no issues found) | 36 |
| Files needing attention | 24 |
| Total data size | 51.4 KB |

## Wrong file extension (header does not match filename) (4 files)

- **Likely cause:** A browser, portal, or script saved a web page (HTML) or a different file type under the original document or photo name.
- **Safe next step:** Test opening a copy with the detected file type (for example rename a copy to .html), or re-download from the original source.

| File | Size | What the scan saw |
|---|---|---|
| `client-proposals/meadowbrook-clinic-sow.docx` | 738 B | Named .docx, but the contents are a web page (HTML) |
| `finance/2026-10-merchant-statement.pdf` | 737 B | Named .pdf, but the contents are a web page (HTML) |
| `photos/catalog-hero-banner.png` | 696 B | Named .png, but the contents are a JPEG photo |
| `photos/trade-show-badge-photo.jpg` | 826 B | Named .jpg, but the contents are a PDF |
```

## What the scanner checks

| Check | What it detects | Why it happens in real transfers |
|---|---|---|
| Extension vs magic bytes | `.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx`, `.pdf`, `.jpg`, `.png`, `.gif`, `.zip`, `.doc`, `.xls`, `.ppt`, `.rtf`, `.html`, `.xml` whose leading bytes do not match their extension | A portal session timed out and saved an HTML sign-in page as `.docx`/`.pdf`, or someone renamed a PDF as `.jpg` |
| Zero-byte files | Files with `size === 0` | Copy created the destination directory entry before the transfer stalled or was cancelled |
| All-zero-byte files | Non-empty files where every byte is `0x00` | Disk space was pre-allocated before a USB drive disconnected or sync failed |
| Truncated files | ZIP/Office files missing an End-of-Central-Directory (`PK\x05\x06`) record, PDFs missing `%%EOF`, JPEGs missing `FFD9` (camera metadata, Samsung trailers and motion-photo video stored after it are recognised, not flagged), PNGs missing `IEND` | Network drop or interrupted copy stopped mid-stream after writing the header |
| Cloud placeholder stubs | `.icloud`, `.url`, `.webloc`, `.gdoc`, `.gsheet`, `.gslides`, `.dropbox` files, or tiny (`<= 512 B`) docs/images containing cloud-sync stub text | Online-only shortcuts or Files On-Demand stubs were copied instead of downloaded contents |
| Path length over 260 chars | Relative or full paths exceeding 260 characters | Deeply nested client folders exceed Windows `MAX_PATH`, blocking Explorer and older Office apps |
| Invalid Windows names | Path segments with `< > : " \| ? *`, control chars, trailing dots/spaces, or reserved device names (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`-`COM9`, `LPT1`-`LPT9`) | Files copied from macOS, Linux, or web archives that Windows refuses to open or copy |
| Password-protected files | PDFs containing `/Encrypt`, OLE2 Office containers with `EncryptionInfo`/`EncryptedPackage`, or ZIP entries with bit-0 encryption set (never opened or decrypted) | Client or staff encrypted the file intentionally before archiving |
| Exact duplicates | Non-empty, non-all-zero files sharing an identical SHA-256 hash | Repeated copy attempts or merged backup folders left identical copies across directories |

*Note on invalid Windows filenames:* `checkPathAndName` is verified against 16 invalid filename cases in [`test/detectors.test.js`](test/detectors.test.js), rather than written into `samples/broken-copy/`, because Windows NTFS rejects creating literal `< > : " | ? *` filenames and reserved device names on disk.

## What comes out

Running `npm run report` writes three files into `output/`:

- [`output/triage-report.md`](output/triage-report.md) — grouped Markdown report with summary counts, likely cause, safe next step, and affected file tables
- [`output/triage-report.html`](output/triage-report.html) — self-contained, print-friendly HTML report with summary cards and clickable issue sections
- [`output/triage-report.csv`](output/triage-report.csv) — full RFC 4180 CSV inventory of every scanned file (including healthy files, byte sizes, detected headers, and SHA-256 hashes)

## How it is tested

`npm test` runs 12 tests across two files using Node's built-in `node:test` runner:

- [`test/detectors.test.js`](test/detectors.test.js) tests each detector individually (magic bytes, all-zero buffers, extension mismatches including encrypted OLE2 Office exceptions, truncation markers, cloud stubs, encryption flags, 260/261-char paths, and Windows-rejected names).
- [`test/triage.test.js`](test/triage.test.js) generates a fresh 60-file synthetic tree into a temporary directory, snapshots every file path, size, and SHA-256 before and after `scanDirectory`, verifies the tree is untouched (read-only), and reconciles every file's detected issues 100% against `truth.json` with zero false positives across all 36 healthy files.

## Run it

Requires Node.js 20 or newer (uses Node built-ins only; no external dependencies).

```sh
npm ci
npm test            # 12 unit and reconciliation tests
npm run generate    # creates 60 synthetic files in samples/broken-copy/ and samples/truth.json
npm run report      # scans samples/broken-copy/ and writes output/triage-report.{md,html,csv}
```

To scan your own folder in read-only mode:

```sh
node src/run.js --in path/to/folder --out reports
```

## Layout

```text
src/detectors.js    magic-byte, truncation, stub, encryption, path/name detectors
src/scanner.js      read-only recursive directory walker and SHA-256 deduplicator
src/report.js       Markdown, HTML, and CSV report writers
src/run.js          CLI entry point (--in, --out)
src/sample.js       deterministic builders for synthetic healthy and broken files
src/generate.js     writes samples/broken-copy/ and samples/truth.json
test/               unit and truth-reconciliation tests (node:test)
samples/truth.json  expected findings for the 60-file synthetic dataset
output/             committed sample reports (.md, .html, .csv)
```
